framings.text: I think this is about helping the next person judge what was checked before trying Tinkery, while keeping small edits and private pre-PR thinking lightweight.

I think this is about a PR review experience only: show clear evidence for each check, avoid repeated entry, and let people reject unhelpful questions without seeing them again. Private scratch work stays outside the handover.

outcome: When someone reviews a Tinkery change, they can quickly tell what evidence exists: real-model evidence, stub mechanics, and the operator's own recognition. Small edits need little or no repeated detail. Unhelpful questions stay dismissed. Private pre-PR thinking does not become a handover.

questions.text: Should the desired experience cover both private pre-PR thinking and PR review, or only PR review? The person defining the goal decides.

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: keep a brief receipt in the PR thread
alternatives.benefit: The next person can see the evidence beside the change, if the PR thread supports concise reused links.
alternatives.cost: The change owner must keep the receipt accurate.
alternatives.undo_cost: Removing receipts could make past checks harder to review.

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: maintain shared check history and link to it from the PR
alternatives.benefit: Repeated checks and small edits may need less new entry, if the shared history stays easy to find.
alternatives.cost: The next person must follow a link and may need more context.
alternatives.undo_cost: Returning to change-by-change records could require rebuilding missing detail.
